network.overall_strategy: Build racemic proline mainly by the only prebiotic route with resolved proline-skeleton intermediates: the surface cyanosulfidic sequence from HCN and acetylene to proline aminonitrile. Add weaker alternative entries through an inferred discharge-Strecker capture of 4-aminobutanal and two hydrothermal branches: a metabolism-inspired glutamate -> P5C -> proline route and a historical arginine pyrolysis route. Because no abiotic synthesis is known to produce L-proline directly, all synthetic branches converge on DL-proline and the target is reached through two alternative phase-behavior amplification steps under prebiotic pool or geothermal cycling. Critical literature-backed intermediates are explicit, while short laboratory substeps inside the cyanosulfidic sequence are bundled into net transformations to stay within the requested graph size. Detection-only extraterrestrial occurrences were not promoted to standalone pathways because they document inventory, not a resolved terrestrial mechanism.

reactions.name: Cu(I)-catalyzed coupling of hydrogen cyanide and acetylene to acrylonitrile

conditions.other: anoxic stream-fed or evaporitic pools; localized impact-carbide acetylene source; staged reagent delivery likely required

reactions.mechanism: Cu(I)-mediated coupling of cyanide with acetylene generates the vinyl nitrile acrylonitrile.
reactions.reasoning: Patel et al. (2015) identified Cu(I)-catalyzed HCN-acetylene coupling as the entry to the proline branch. This step is chemically strong but geochemically local because both acetylene supply and Cu availability are contested at planetary scale, and the broader cyanosulfidic setting also depends on cyanide persistence and staged delivery (Patel et al., 2015; Ranjan et al., 2018; Todd et al., 2024).

reactions.name: Aza-Michael addition of ammonia to acrylonitrile
reactions.mechanism: Ammonia adds across the activated C=C bond of acrylonitrile to give beta-aminopropionitrile.
reactions.reasoning: Patel et al. (2015) explicitly used ammonia addition to acrylonitrile to access beta-aminopropionitrile, a key branch-point precursor for proline. No special mineral catalyst is required; the chemistry is a straightforward aza-Michael addition favored in NH3-bearing mildly basic waters (Patel et al., 2015).

reactions.name: UV/H2S homologation and cyclization of beta-aminopropionitrile to gamma-butyrothiolactam

conditions.other: UV irradiation; laboratory analog uses 254 nm; sulfide-rich shallow water; net sequence passes through aldehyde, cyanohydrin, and hydroxythioamide intermediates

reactions.mechanism: Net cyanosulfidic sequence: nitrile photoreduction to the aldehyde, HCN addition to the cyanohydrin, sulfide conversion to thioamide chemistry, then photodeoxygenation and ring closure to the cyclic thioamide.
reactions.reasoning: Patel et al. (2015) resolved the downstream nitrile-to-aldehyde, cyanohydrin, thioamide, and cyclization chemistry leading to gamma-butyrothiolactam. This node compresses those observed substeps into one net transformation to keep the network within the requested size. H2S can act as the stoichiometric photoreductant without Cu photoredox acceleration, but the need for sulfidic anions and laboratory 254 nm UV remains a major environmental critique (Patel et al., 2015; Ranjan et al., 2018).

reactions.name: Cu-photoredox-assisted UV/H2S homologation and cyclization of beta-aminopropionitrile to gamma-butyrothiolactam

conditions.other: UV irradiation; laboratory analog uses 254 nm; HS-/H2S serves as reductant while copper accelerates the photoredox sequence

reactions.mechanism: The same net cyanosulfidic homologation as rxn_003 occurs, but Cu(I)/Cu(II) mediates faster photoredox turnover during reduction and cyclization.
reactions.reasoning: Patel et al. (2015) reported that Cu(I)-Cu(II) photoredox can accelerate the cyanosulfidic network. It is treated here as a distinct pathway because copper changes the redox mediation while preserving the same net chemistry. Cu scarcity and sulfide complexation mean this version is plausible only in localized Cu-bearing surface settings (Patel et al., 2015; Ranjan et al., 2018).

reactions.name: Photoreductive conversion of gamma-butyrothiolactam to proline aminonitrile

conditions.other: UV irradiation; inferred cyclic imine intermediate; HCN capture furnishes the alpha-aminonitrile

reactions.mechanism: Further sulfide-driven photoreduction and desulfurization generates a cyclic imine that undergoes Strecker-type HCN addition to give pyrrolidine-2-carbonitrile.
reactions.reasoning: Patel et al. (2015) reported conversion of the cyclic thioamide to proline alpha-aminonitrile in 32% over the final two steps; the intervening cyclic imine was inferred rather than isolated. Ritson (2021) noted that proline aminonitrile is unusually resistant to retro-Strecker reversion relative to acyclic aminonitriles, making this product especially durable under fluctuating NH3 or pH (Patel et al., 2015; Ritson, 2021).

reactions.name: Hydrolysis of proline aminonitrile to DL-proline

conditions.other: prolonged aqueous hydrolysis during wet-dry or geothermal cycling; likely proceeds through an amide intermediate

reactions.mechanism: Stepwise nitrile hydration and hydrolysis converts the aminonitrile into the amino acid carboxylate.
reactions.reasoning: Patel et al. (2015) stopped at the aminonitrile and did not report a proline hydrolysis yield, so this is chemically expected but quantitatively unverified for that system. It is retained because aminonitrile hydrolysis is the canonical route from Strecker products to amino acids, and proline aminonitrile is comparatively persistent rather than strongly retroconverting (Patel et al., 2015; Ritson, 2021).

reactions.name: Strecker-type capture of 4-aminobutanal to proline aminonitrile

conditions.other: electric discharge not modeled explicitly; 4-aminobutanal represents a discharge-derived precursor pool and cyclizes to 1-pyrroline in water

reactions.mechanism: 4-Aminobutanal cyclizes to 1-pyrroline, which then undergoes HCN addition to yield pyrrolidine-2-carbonitrile.
reactions.reasoning: Ring et al. (1972) reported proline in Miller-type discharge products, but no 4-aminobutanal or proline-aminonitrile sequence was isolated. This step is therefore an inferred mechanistic reconstruction from general Strecker logic rather than a directly demonstrated prebiotic transformation. Parker et al. (2011) also emphasized that common OPA/NAC analyses miss secondary amines such as proline, so later non-detections are not decisive (Ring et al., 1972; Parker et al., 2011).

reactions.name: Activated reduction and cyclization of glutamate to pyrroline-5-carboxylate

conditions.other: alkaline H2-rich vent or subseafloor setting; gamma-carboxylate activation is required before reduction; spontaneous cyclization of glutamate-5-semialdehyde is implicit

reactions.mechanism: A speculative surface-mediated activation of the gamma-carboxylate is followed by reduction to glutamate-5-semialdehyde, which then cyclizes nearly completely to P5C.
reactions.reasoning: Hydrothermal and metal-mediated reductive amination can generate glutamate from alpha-ketoglutarate, but the glutamate -> GSA/P5C step has no prebiotic demonstration and is the main bottleneck of the metabolism-first route. It is included as a chemically motivated but explicitly speculative step because biology spends energy to activate this carboxylate, whereas prebiotic analogs remain unknown; once GSA forms, cyclization to P5C is expected to be facile (Huber & Wachtershauser, 2003; Kitadai et al., 2019; Kaur et al., 2024; Smith & Greenberg, 1956; Fichman et al., 2015).

reactions.name: Reduction of pyrroline-5-carboxylate to DL-proline

conditions.other: moderate-temperature alkaline vent chemistry; proposed metal-mediated imine reduction under H2-rich conditions

reactions.mechanism: Metal-assisted reduction of the cyclic imine in P5C yields racemic proline.
reactions.reasoning: P5C reduction is chemically easier than the preceding glutamate carboxylate reduction, and related pyrroline carboxylates are readily reduced in the laboratory, but no prebiotic H2/Ni, Fe0, or FeS example has been reported for proline. This node is therefore speculative but a priority experimental target for protometabolic frameworks (Smith & Greenberg, 1956; Fichman et al., 2015; Kaur et al., 2024).

reactions.name: Hydrothermal conversion of arginine to DL-proline

conditions.other: subseafloor hydrothermal pyrolysis at moderate temperatures to limit amino-acid destruction; ornithine and pyrroline-like intermediates are implicit

reactions.mechanism: Net deguanidination, deamination, and intramolecular cyclization through ornithine-like and pyrroline-like intermediates gives proline.
reactions.reasoning: Vallentyne (1968) reported proline among aqueous arginine pyrolysis products, making this the only nonenzymatic hint of an ornithine or arginine branch to proline. The mechanism and even the historical product assignment remain uncertain, and modern re-analysis has been recommended; moreover arginine itself is a difficult prebiotic feedstock, so this branch is included only as a weak, testable alternative (Vallentyne, 1968; Korner et al., 2021).

reactions.name: Eutectic phase enrichment of DL-proline to L-proline

conditions.other: requires a small initial L-bias; node represents the L-enriched recoverable fraction from dissolution-crystallization cycling

reactions.mechanism: Preferential crystallization and solid-solution partitioning enrich the recoverable liquid or dissolved fraction in the L-enantiomer while racemate remains in the solid phase.
reactions.reasoning: No abiotic synthesis route yields L-proline directly, so a separate chiral amplification step is required. Proline is the best-studied amino acid for physical amplification: Klussmann et al. (2006) showed that solution ee is pinned near the eutectic composition, reaching about 54-58% ee in methanol or ethanol systems. The more dramatic CHCl3 cosolvate case is not prebiotic, so this network retains only the more geochemically defensible eutectic principle and treats the required seed ee as an environmental condition rather than a separate node (Klussmann et al., 2006; Blackmond, 2019).

reactions.name: Sequential phase-behavior amplification of DL-proline to L-proline

conditions.other: requires a small initial L-bias; repeated dissolution and recrystallization across phase boundaries under geothermal cycling

reactions.mechanism: Serial partial dissolution and recrystallization under changing phase conditions ratchets a small L-excess upward in the recoverable fraction.
reactions.reasoning: This second chirality route is more speculative than the direct eutectic step, but it is chemically motivated by modeled sequential amplification across changing conglomerate and racemic-compound regimes. It is included because direct asymmetric proline synthesis is unknown, and cyclic physical enrichment is geochemically more plausible than the nonprebiotic CHCl3 cosolvate system even though it remains untested specifically for proline (Sharma, 2023; Blackmond, 2019).

pathway_evaluations.feedback: P1 is the strongest and most literature-aligned branch because rxn_001 and rxn_002 match the Patel cyanosulfidic entry to the proline skeleton. The explicit network then breaks conservation at the core: rxn_003 and rxn_005 are ground-truth UNBALANCED bundled transformations, and rxn_006 is UNBALANCED and should include 2 H2O as reactants and NH3 as product. Literature support is also strongest only up to mol_008; the aminonitrile hydrolysis to proline is not quantified here. rxn_011 reflects real proline phase behavior, but it is a resolution step rather than a full DL to L conversion and needs a seed ee plus an explicit D-rich companion phase. Good route to proline aminonitrile; not yet a validated route to isolated L-proline.
suggestions: Decompose rxn_003 into explicit aldehyde, cyanohydrin, hydroxythioamide, and thiolactam substeps with byproducts.
For rxn_005, either include sulfur coproducts explicitly or use a balanced shorthand such as mol_007 + mol_001 -> mol_008 + S with H2S moved to conditions.
Rewrite rxn_006 as mol_008 + 2 H2O -> mol_013 + NH3 and report hydrolysis conditions or yield.
Model rxn_011 as a eutectic or evaporation-crystallization module with seed ee, temperature or solvent, and the D-rich phase, or rename the product as L-enriched proline.

pathway_evaluations.feedback: P2 keeps the same credible early cyanosulfidic backbone as P1, but rxn_003, rxn_005, and rxn_006 remain unbalanced and therefore invalid as written. The final step is weaker than in P1: rxn_012 is a speculative sequential amplification module rather than an experimentally established prebiotic resolution of proline. As drawn, this path does not convincingly deliver L-proline beyond a hypothetical enrichment scenario.
suggestions: Apply the P1 balancing fixes to rxn_003, rxn_005, and rxn_006.
Replace rxn_012 with experimentally grounded proline eutectic data or explicitly keep it as a speculative amplification model.
If only partial enrichment is justified, rename mol_014 as L-enriched proline and add the D-rich companion phase.

pathway_evaluations.feedback: P3 follows the Cu-assisted Patel variant and is reasonable on stated conditions, but Cu acceleration does not fix the reaction specification. rxn_004 and rxn_005 are ground-truth UNBALANCED bundled nets, rxn_006 should include 2 H2O and NH3, and the literature support still weakens after mol_008 because hydrolysis to proline is unquantified. rxn_011 again represents enrichment or resolution behavior, not a complete synthetic conversion to L-proline. This remains a partial route to racemic proline precursors rather than a validated route to L-proline.
suggestions: Keep Cu photoredox as a condition, but split rxn_004 into balanced Patel substeps instead of a lumped net reaction.
Balance rxn_005 with explicit sulfur coproducts or a balanced net shorthand.
Rewrite rxn_006 with water and ammonia and report whether hydrolysis is surface, thermal, or mineral-assisted.
Replace the Biochemical label on rxn_011 with an explicit prebiotic eutectic or evaporative setting.

pathway_evaluations.feedback: P4 inherits the same chemically sensible entry from Patel chemistry as P3, but the explicit core still violates conservation in rxn_004 and rxn_005, and rxn_006 still omits the water and ammonia required for hydrolysis. The final rxn_012 step is even less secure than rxn_011 because sequential phase-behavior amplification is not demonstrated here for proline under prebiotic conditions. The route is coherent as a hypothesis, not as a validated synthesis to L-proline.
suggestions: Apply the P3 balancing fixes to rxn_004, rxn_005, and rxn_006.
Downgrade rxn_012 to a theoretical chirality module unless a proline-specific prebiotic demonstration is cited.
Model the D-rich companion phase and seed ee or rename the endpoint as L-enriched proline.

pathway_evaluations.feedback: P5 is chemically conceivable as an inferred Strecker capture of 4-aminobutanal or 1-pyrroline, and rxn_007 is close to correct if H2O is added as product. But the mechanism is inferred rather than experimentally resolved in discharge chemistry, the provenance of mol_009 is not justified in the graph, rxn_006 is still unbalanced and unquantified, and rxn_011 does not fully resolve a racemate to pure L-proline. This is a weak alternative entry, not a demonstrated pathway.
suggestions: Rewrite rxn_007 as mol_009 + mol_001 -> mol_008 + H2O and consider adding a 1-pyrroline intermediate.
Justify how mol_009 is generated and transferred into the surface aqueous setting.
Rewrite rxn_006 as mol_008 + 2 H2O -> mol_013 + NH3 and treat rxn_011 as enrichment rather than full conversion.

pathway_evaluations.feedback: P6 has the same inferred Strecker logic as P5 and the same near-fixable balance issue in rxn_007, but it compounds that with the weaker final step rxn_012. The graph still lacks a justified source for mol_009, rxn_006 still needs explicit hydrolysis stoichiometry, and the chirality module is too speculative to claim target achievement. At best this is a conjectural route to some L-enrichment, not to validated L-proline.
suggestions: Use the balanced form of rxn_007 with H2O as product and add a 1-pyrroline intermediate if possible.
Rewrite rxn_006 as mol_008 + 2 H2O -> mol_013 + NH3.
Keep rxn_012 explicitly speculative unless a proline-specific sequential amplification study under prebiotic conditions is cited.

pathway_evaluations.feedback: P7 does not match current experimental support. The literature supports glutamate formation under some prebiotic hydrothermal conditions, but not glutamate to P5C or P5C to proline. rxn_008 is ground-truth UNBALANCED and omits the activation and reductant burden of carboxylate reduction; rxn_009 is UNBALANCED and needs H2 as reactant even before chemical plausibility is considered; rxn_011 still leaves chirality unresolved. This branch should be treated as a hypothesis, not a validated route.
suggestions: Insert activated glutamate or glutamate-5-semialdehyde between mol_010 and mol_011 instead of direct rxn_008.
If a net stoichiometry is kept, rxn_008 needs explicit reductant and water balance and rxn_009 needs H2 as reactant.
Treat this branch as hypothetical and justify transport from hydrothermal formation to the separate phase-enrichment environment.

pathway_evaluations.feedback: P8 is weaker than P7 because it combines an unsupported hydrothermal proline branch with a highly speculative chirality module. rxn_008 remains an unbalanced and chemically uphill carboxylate reduction, rxn_009 still lacks the H2 needed even for stoichiometry, and rxn_012 does not provide a demonstrated prebiotic route from DL-proline to L-proline. This pathway is not currently viable.
suggestions: Add an activated glutamate or glutamate-5-semialdehyde intermediate and explicit redox chemistry for rxn_008 and rxn_009.
Write rxn_009 with H2 as reactant or do not claim a reducing step.
Replace rxn_012 with a cited proline-specific enrichment experiment or keep the endpoint as DL-proline.

pathway_evaluations.feedback: P9 relies on the weakest literature support in the network. Hydrothermal arginine to proline is only a historical degradation report with uncertain product identification. rxn_010 is ground-truth UNBALANCED and omits required coproducts for the lost guanidino fragment; a coproduct such as guanidine or an ornithine-containing degradation network would need to be made explicit. Even if DL-proline were formed, rxn_011 still lacks a complete resolution mechanism to L-proline.
suggestions: Replace rxn_010 with a multistep arginine degradation network including explicit coproducts; guanidine is one plausible net coproduct candidate.
Confirm proline formation and yield with modern analytics before keeping this branch as more than a speculative degradation route.
Model rxn_011 as a geochemical phase-resolution step with seed ee and a D-rich phase, not a simple DL to L conversion.

pathway_evaluations.feedback: P10 combines the least supported synthetic branch with the least supported chirality step. rxn_010 is unbalanced and mechanistically unresolved, and rxn_012 is only a theoretical amplification idea here rather than a demonstrated proline-specific prebiotic process. This pathway does not currently substantiate production of L-proline.
suggestions: Redraw rxn_010 with explicit coproducts or intermediates instead of a single unbalanced arrow.
Relegate the arginine branch to a speculative hypothesis until modern analytical confirmation exists.
Keep rxn_012 explicitly theoretical and include the required seed ee and D-rich companion phase.

evaluation.network_feedback: The network is well framed around the correct literature backbone: the Patel cyanosulfidic route is rightly central, and it is good that meteorite and ice detections were not promoted to mechanistic terrestrial pathways. The graph is connected and uses consistent molecule IDs. However network validity is substantially weakened because 8 of 12 reaction nodes are ground-truth UNBALANCED: rxn_003, rxn_004, rxn_005, rxn_006, rxn_007, rxn_008, rxn_009, and rxn_010. Specific fixes are available for some nodes: rxn_007 needs H2O as product; rxn_009 needs H2 as reactant; rxn_006 should be written as mol_008 + 2 H2O -> mol_013 + NH3; rxn_010 needs explicit coproducts for the lost guanidino fragment, with guanidine being one plausible net coproduct. rxn_005 may need sulfur coproducts or H2S moved from reactants to conditions; a possible shorthand is mol_007 + mol_001 -> mol_008 + S. rxn_003 and rxn_004 cannot be rescued by a simple small-species patch and should be expanded into Patel's explicit aldehyde, cyanohydrin, thioamide, thiolactam, and imine-level substeps. rxn_008 also needs explicit activation and reductant chemistry, not just a one-arrow hydrothermal conversion. The hydrothermal glutamate or P5C and arginine branches are much less supported than the cyanosulfidic branch and should be marked as hypotheses rather than parallel validated routes. Finally, rxn_011 and especially rxn_012 are not full synthetic conversions to L-proline; proline phase behavior can enrich ee only with a seed ee, explicit solvent or eutectic conditions, and a modeled D-enriched companion phase, and the Biochemical environment label should be replaced by explicit prebiotic pool, eutectic, freeze-thaw, or evaporation-crystallization settings. Overall, the network is coherent in concept and literature-aware, but it is not currently a chemically valid or fully target-achieving synthesis network for L-proline.
